Reviewed on the cheap tier at the maintainer's instruction. This PR changes when the adaptive toolpath planner refuses a region and falls back to Offset rings - toolpath generation under AGENTS.md's safety floor - so its review should run at the high tier; treat this pass as a first screen, not the full verdict.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one testing-law item and two notes; no correctness defect found in the code paths I read).

## What looks good

- The refusal is the only behaviour change. The counters are pure reads (`add_geometry` counts `loops()` points) and the step, ring, trial order and early exits are untouched (`grow.rs` diff: the only edits are the `over()` check at the same loop position, and the `add_geometry` / `add_len` calls).
- The #13 length law runs first with the same message (`budget.rs` `over()`, `WORK_MAX * r` check unchanged), so its refusals and the named fallback are unchanged.
- Counting is sequential: no rayon, no hash maps, no threads in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/` (checked). The f64 length sum and the u64 vertex sum are order-fixed. `add_geometry` uses `saturating_add` and `try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)`; no unwrap/expect/panic outside `#[cfg(test)]`.
- The AND is as stated: `budget.rs` `over()` refuses only when `verts > GEOM_MAX && len > GEOM_LEN * r` (both strict). The unit test covers vertices-only and walk-only both staying under.
- `mod.rs` is still 435 lines (no growth). `budget.rs` is 208, `budget_fixtures.rs` 69. The new module carries a provenance line.
- The decisions file records the dropped options with numbers (vertices alone, time-faithful unit, wall clock, trial counts, islanded-only, simplification). The PR body has the table, `Fixes #850`, and a `Changelog:` line.

## Local results (trial merge with origin/main 4c3f7565; no conflicts)

Build: `camcraft-motion` lib tests and integration tests built clean; app `pocket3d_hsm` test binary compiled (heavy bodies not run).

| suite | result | time |
|---|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --lib -- adaptive` (default) | 21 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (heavy: budget fixtures) | 57.6 s |
| `--test adaptive_hsm` (default) | 2 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored | 58.9 s total |
| `--test adaptive_band` (default) | 2 passed | 2.7 s |
| `--test pocket3d_hsm` (motion, default) | 3 passed, 1 ignored (heavy) | 13.0 s |
| `camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm --no-run` | compiles | - |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean | - |

The island pin on this machine, debug: `the_island_is_refused_by_the_geometry_budget_in_seconds` passed in **58.8 s** (the PR body says 46.2 s). Its note: `growing the cleared area ran past its planning budget after 109 revolutions - its rings (~600 k outline vertices worked over ~9 k tool radii ...)`, then `Offset rings cut this pocket instead`.

Not run: the `--ignored` heavy lanes (per the maintainer's instruction; the author ran them in release on ecb54b7f), the release tier, and the app bore test body.

## Requested before merge

1. **Island pin is at the default-suite time limit** (`crates/motion/tests/adaptive_hsm.rs`, `the_island_is_refused_by_the_geometry_budget_in_seconds`, ~line 390). It took 58.8 s debug here, and AGENTS.md "Testing" says a test over ~60 s in debug moves to the heavy lane (with the lane named in the ignore reason) or gets a slimmer fixture. Either mark it `#[ignore = "heavy lane: ... (~60 s debug)"]` and run it in release, or cut its cost. Its pin is valuable, so the lane move is the simpler fix. The author's 46 s figure should be corrected in the PR body.

## Notes (not blocking)

- **The bore digest is printed, not asserted** (`crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`, digest block in `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`). Byte identity with main rests on the author's run plus the no-refusal assertion. `DefaultHasher` is not guaranteed stable across Rust releases, so asserting the digest would need a golden file or a Rust-version note. The heavy-lane no-refusal assert covers the 5 k r threshold at the bore's 2.6 k r, which is a 1.93x margin. I judge that acceptable; a digest golden would be stronger.
- **Bore walk and rotary counts are not pinned in the default suite.** The counter is crate-private to motion, so the bore (1.93x on walk) only gets its heavy-lane no-refusal assert. A future change that pushes the bore past 5 k r would fail that heavy test, not a default test. Acceptable, but expose a `pub(crate)` hook if #845 changes the constants.
- **NaN length is no longer poisoning the sum** (`budget.rs` `add_len`, filter `is_finite() && > 0`). Before, a NaN revolution made the length sum NaN, so later revolutions were never refused by #13. Now they can be. This is a degenerate-input case, so it is a refusal-decision change only where the old code was silently wrong, but it should be stated in the PR body.
- **Refusal wording** (`budget.rs` `over_geometry`): "over 600 k" after "~9 k tool radii" reads as if it refers to the walk. Consider "over the 600 k vertex budget". The text itself is accurate for heavy-and-long, and the caller appends the named Offset-rings fallback, which the test checks.
- Process: no `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` or process-file change in this PR; none needed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Delta review on the cheap tier at the maintainer's instruction. This PR changes when the adaptive toolpath planner refuses a region - toolpath generation under AGENTS.md's safety floor - so the high-tier review is still owed before merge; this pass is a first screen of the review round only.

**Verdict:** No blocker in the delta, and the requested change (island pin to the heavy lane, with a fast twin) is resolved. Not merge-ready yet: the high-tier review is still owed.

**What looks good**
- Requested change: the full island pin is `#[ignore = "heavy lane: release --ignored ..."]` (`crates/motion/tests/adaptive_hsm.rs` around line 394), with its assertions kept: the named refusal, the count bound `600.0..=620.0` (a real bound: past 600 k by at most about one revolution), the Offset rings chained and finite, and the verifier silent.
- The fast twin `machining2d::adaptive::budget::fixtures::the_island_trips_lowered_geometry_limits_by_name` is a real test of the refusal path. It runs `plan_within`'s own growth loop on the island with `Work::with_limits(20_000, 200.0)`, asserts the refusal names both limits and states both caps, and asserts `passes` and `joins` are empty.
- The `#[test]` count did not drop: +2 (fast twin, NaN test); the ignored island pin still counts.
- Seam: `Work::with_limits` is `#[cfg(test)]`. `plan_within` is a private fn in `adaptive/mod.rs` with one production caller, `plan()`, which passes `budget::Work::default()` (`GEOM_MAX`, `GEOM_LEN`, the same constants the previous head read directly). Production behaviour is identical to e8def282.
- `push_walk` moved from `mod.rs` to `grow.rs` with the same body (now `pub(super)`, using `super::front::dist`). It is a move. `mod.rs` 431 lines, `grow.rs` 331.
- The refusal text is pinned in `budget.rs` (tests, about line 224), `budget_fixtures.rs` (line 91) and `adaptive_hsm.rs` (line 405-408, which parses the count after "both limits passed, ~"). No other pins of the old wording in `crates/` or `docs/`.
- The bore's exact counts (5530 moves, 5497 planar feeds, 600 arcs) plus the per-level strategy are a sound pin: any planner change that moves the bore path fails it, which is the intent. The comment in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` (about lines 101-103) says the counts are re-measured and why. Heavy lane only; read, not run here.

**Local results** (trial merge of `05cf06e9` with `origin/main` `77b897c8`: clean, no conflicts; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` in the review worktree)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- adaptive`: 23 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the fixtures pin, heavy lane); suite finished in 54.6 s.
- The fast pin alone: ok, 2.4 s in debug (`island at lowered limits: 2.4 s`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test adaptive_hsm`: 1 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored; test time 10.4 s, about 27 s wall including compile.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test adaptive_band`: 2 passed, 0 failed; 2.6 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the app `pocket3d_hsm` bore test (heavy, ignored); no `--ignored` lanes.

**Requested before merge** (body wording, for the author; the high-tier pass may add to this)
1. PR body, first section: "no wall clock, not even as a backstop". The Pinning section says the island pin keeps "a loose wall-clock backstop: 600 s debug, 60 s release". Say the budget itself is clock-free, and the test keeps a backstop.
2. PR body says the Offset-ring fallback is "pinned fast by `adaptive_band`". `adaptive_band` pins the fallback for an up-front (#13) refusal through the same `refused` path, not the geometry refusal. Say that precisely: the geometry fallback is pinned in full only by the heavy island pin.
3. PR body gives the fast twin as "1.8 s debug"; measured here at 2.4 s. Update it.
4. PR body gives the island release time as 18.7-20.5 s in one place and 18.7-22.0 s in another. Harmonise.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- Refusal text: "~600.0 k outline vertices processed (limit 600 k) and ~9.4 k tool radii of path (limit 5.0 k)" reads plainly by its clauses. "outline vertices" and "tool radii" are internal units; "cutter radii" might read better to a user. "600.0 k" against "600 k" is a formatting mismatch. Both optional.
- The bore counts were run on 6b89fdf8 per the body, not on the final head. The later commit only touches the island test's parsing, so this is acceptable; say so in the body.
- The trial merge brings in main's own changes (AGENTS.md, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, process files). None of that is this PR's; the PR itself touches `crates/` and `docs/decisions/` only (no build.rs, `.github`, scripts or dependencies).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 05cf06e916d3a1f04b4f87d125d8f7f4dccca2ec -->
High-tier review (the one the two earlier cheap-tier passes said was owed), on head 05cf06e9 trial-merged with current `origin/main` (d47a306, merged cleanly).

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blocker found.

## What looks good

- **No partial toolpath on a refusal.** `grow.rs:150` checks `Work::over` at the top of every revolution and returns `Grown::Refused`. `mod.rs:272-275` then returns `AdaptivePlan::default()` with only `refused` and the notes set: no passes, no joins. `pocket_hsm` hands the area to the Offset rings by name, as with the #13 refusals. The fast twin asserts this on the planner's own loop.
- **Law 3 only tightens.** Law 2 (`len > WORK_MAX * r`) is checked first with its message unchanged (`budget.rs` `over()`), and law 3 is an extra `&&` refusal. Nothing that main refused now passes, and the 30 k r cap on the hang in #850 still stands.
- **A false refusal needs both counts.** It needs more than 600 k vertices AND more than 5 k r of walk (both strict). The bore (1.14 M, 2.6 k r) cannot trip it, and its path is pinned by exact move, planar and arc counts plus the strategy list.
- **The counters do not change the path.** They are pure reads: `add_geometry` counts the `loops()` points of regions already computed, and `add_len` replaces the old `Cell<f64>` sum. Neither changes trial order, steps or exits, so a plan that is not refused is the same as on main.
- **The counts are deterministic.** They are sequential, with no wall clock: `saturating_add` and `try_from(..).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` on the u64, and `r.max(1e-9)` on the division (`r > 0` is validated in `plan_within`).
- **Prime Directive:** no `unwrap/expect/panic!` outside tests. The NaN / inf / non-positive guard in `add_len` closes a real hole: a NaN used to switch law 2 off for the rest of the plan. It is pinned by `a_nan_length_neither_refuses_nor_disables_the_budget`.
- **The refusal is named in plain English** and states both limits. Example from my run: "...its outline is too detailed and its path too long to plan in seconds (an island?): both limits passed, ~600.0 k outline vertices processed (limit 600 k) and ~9.4 k tool radii of path (limit 5.0 k); ... - Offset rings cut this pocket instead".
- **`#[test]` count:** motion 755 -> 760 (+5), app `pocket3d_hsm` unchanged (2). No test is removed. Both new ignores name their lane (`heavy lane: release --ignored (...)`).
- **Process:** a provenance line on `budget_fixtures.rs`; the decision is in `docs/decisions/850-adaptive-geometry-budget.md`; no `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot, golden or process-file changes. `mod.rs` went from 435 to 431 lines. The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #850`.

## Local results (merged with main, Windows, own target)

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` | plan: motion lib + adaptive_band + adaptive_hsm + pocket3d_hsm; app pocket3d_hsm build-only (its changed fn is heavy lane) |
| motion lib (debug) | 189 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored |
| motion `adaptive_band` | 2 passed |
| motion `adaptive_hsm` | 1 passed, 5 ignored |
| motion `pocket3d_hsm` | 3 passed, 1 ignored |
| `budget::*` + fast twin + `a_channel_is_grown...` by name | 5 passed (twin included) |
| heavy, release: `adaptive_hsm::the_island_is_refused_by_the_geometry_budget_in_seconds` | **ok, 21.8 s**: refused after 109 revs at ~600.0 k / ~9.4 k r, named, rings cut it, verifier silent |
| heavy, release: `budget::fixtures::the_fixtures_that_grow_today_stay_under_the_geometry_budget` | ok, 16.6 s: slot 252,528 (0.42 of the budget), channel 175,217 (0.29) |
| clippy `-p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm -D warnings` | clean (compiles the changed bore test) |

Not run: the app bore heavy test (`pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_...`, ~210 s release plus a release app build), the rotary / boss / stepped-block heavy lanes, and the release tier. For those I relied on the author's heavy-lane table at ecb54b7f; the counters and limits are unchanged since that head.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes (non-blocking)

1. **A residual false-refusal case.** A pocket with a finely tessellated outline like the bore's, but large enough to walk past 5 k r, would be over both limits. It would be refused to the named Offset rings where main grows it. Main would take many minutes on it: the bore spends ~200 s at 2.6 k r, and time grows about with the square of the vertices per trial. So the outcome is a named fallback, never wrong output. Worth keeping in view in #882, which makes the per-trial geometry cheaper and could then raise `GEOM_LEN`.
2. **Law 3 does not bound everything (not a regression).** It does not bound the heavy-but-short regime (the bore's 200 s), nor the trials inside one revolution: `over()` runs once per revolution, and `step_search` may run several trials before that. The star-cell morph and the engagement-front paths (`core_spiral` / `open_rounds`) are not under it either. All of this predates the PR and is outside #850. #882 covers the first.
3. **#845 interaction.** As the body says, #845's held fix roughly doubles growth work and would push the slot and the rotary levels toward 600 k. The 1.9x margin pins (`adaptive::tests`, the heavy fixtures test) will fail there and force the re-measure. That is the intended tripwire.
4. **The bore pin's exact counts are brittle on purpose.** `pocket3d_hsm.rs` asserts `(5530, 5497, 600)`, so any later planner change must re-measure and say why. The comment says so. This is fine, but it is a heavy-lane test, so a drift shows only at a cut or in a heavy run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
